title: Django, a Pittsburgh bar and refusing to be served as a favour
summary: Greer recalls a Pittsburgh bar refusing service to a Black customer and his stand for dignity.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: None. Little tiny. So I body-guarded him. I remember one time we played a concert in Pittsburgh. So he, a French boy living here, so he say, "Come on, Sonny, we go have a drink." I say, all right. So we go in this high class joint, we stand up at the bar, cat don't pay him no mind. So, you know, French hot, so he knock on the bar. "Service". And the guy says, "I can serve you, Mister," but he wouldn't serve me. "What'd he say that for?" Had to drag the guy out of the bar. He wanted to create a scene. I said, "Man, it's nothing. Forget it." He say, oh, a lot of French. I don't know what the hell he was saying but I know it was hot.

So the guy, after he found out who we were, he apologized. "Come in." So I say, "We don't want to come in your bar, Mister. You don't do me no favor, I spend the money. I owe you nothing. Forget it. You drink it." Anyway, he couldn't even give it to me. I'm hot now. So we go, go back down Wiley Avenue (unintelligible) Ball! Ball! Ball! But you're a you see, /the average thing the guys make, they make a mistake. They see a colored guy so right away they category them all as one. They don't give you any consideration that you have

more brains than they do. So ain't no cat, ain't ever born a cat could think he'd do me a favor when I'm spending my money. Uh-uh. Because I come in a gentleman, I treat this place with respect. So what am I? So I won't bother about it. Understand what I mean?

I never in my life -- I look back sometimes, it gets frightening. I never in my life took water from nobody. Nobody, and I've been in some of the worst dives, it frightens me now, in the world. But I always stood up for my rights and dignity, anywhere, in Europe and America. All you got to say, you know, "Okay, I see you later." (Laughter.) Oh, I could write a book on some of the episodes in my life. It would be a best seller.
